properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 30 at 7:36PM MST until October 30 at 7:45PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
The Flood Advisory will expire at 745 PM MST this evening for a
portion of south central Arizona, including the following area,
Surprise, Sun City West, Beardsley.

The heavy rain has ended. Flooding is no longer expected to pose a
threat. Please continue to heed remaining road closures.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued October 30 at 7:29PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
At 729 PM MST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Downtown Phoenix moving northeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 30 mph and half inch size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Phoenix, Scottsdale, Paradise Valley, Piestewa Peak Park, Camelback
Mountain, Scottsdale Airport, Sky Harbor Airport and Arizona State
Fairgrounds.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.
properties.area: Deer Valley; Central Phoenix; North Phoenix/Glendale; Scottsdale/Paradise Valley; East Valley; Fountain Hills/East Mesa

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued October 30 at 9:29PM CDT by NWS Quad Cities IA IL
properties.description:
At 928 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking line of heavy rain along a
line extending from near Gladstone to New London. This line of heavy
rain were nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Minor flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Slowing or redirecting of traffic due to ponding or flowing
water. Closure of waterfront access due to flooding.

Locations impacted include...
Burlington, West Burlington, Danville, Middletown, Gulf Port,
Beaverdale, Des Moines County Fairgrounds, Starr's Cave Park and
Preserve, and Prairie Grove.

Radar rainfall estimates of 2 to 3 inches have fallen and an
additional 1 inch of rain is possible.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

If the heavy rain continues, a flash flood warning may be needed.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued October 30 at 7:23PM MST until October 30 at 10:15PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
At 723 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
0.75 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up
to 0.75 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Scottsdale, Paradise Valley and Scottsdale Airport.

This includes AZ Route 101 between mile markers 36 and 43.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued October 30 at 9:11PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
At 911 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong shower near
Martha, moving north at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Altus, Blair, Martha, and Altus Air Force Base.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Conditions are favorable for the formation of funnel clouds, but the
threat posed by these funnel clouds is low. Most funnel clouds will
not reach the ground. If they do, weak tornadoes with brief wind
gusts in excess of 50 MPH may occur.

If you observe a funnel cloud or one is reported in your area, move
indoors and stay away from windows.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 30 at 9:02PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds and downstream tidal effects on the St
John River are slowing flow at Astor.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Friday the stage was 3.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Friday was 3.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.6 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon EDT.

- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded

properties.description:

* WHEN...Until 900 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the upper Santa Clara River in Pine Valley
down stream to just below Baker Reservoir is imminent or occurring.
The USGS gauge on the Santa Clara River peaked at 613 CFS at 1pm
with flows coming down gradually, but high flows are expected to
continue with additional rainfall moving into the area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 429 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
slow moving thunderstorms with very heavy rainfall across the
warned area. Between 1.25 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
The Santa Clara River through Pine Valley and down stream to just
below Baker Reservoir.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, roads and normally dry washes is likely. The heavy rains will
likely trigger rockslides, mudslides and debris flows in steep
terrain, especially in and around these areas.
